Inglewood, California
  February 6, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  February 6, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 1, 2024, in the amount of $2,521,192.43, are hereby allowed, and the City
  Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to
  certify upon said registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

160  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – SUZANNE M. MALDONADO GARCIA. Staff report
  dated February 6, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members
  authorize payment of an invoice submitted by Suzanne M. Maldonado Garcia, for providing
  live entertainment for the City’s Annual Dia De Los Muertos Festival on October 28, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $2,050. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  ENCROACHMENT PERMIT AND COVENANT AGREEMENT NO. 24-112
  APPROVED – JEFFERSON WESTCHESTER, LLC. Staff report dated February 6,
  2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve the
  subject Encroachment Permit and Covenant Agreement with Jefferson Westchester, LLC,
  to install certain temporary tiebacks in the City’s right-of-way, affecting the development
  of Real Property located at 939 Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood, California.
 February 6, 2024

  Louis Atwell, Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director, provided a brief overview
  regarding the subject Encroachment Permit and Covenant Agreement, including the
  definition of tiebacks.

  Following discussion, it was moved by Council Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the City Council does hereby approve Encroachment Permit and
  Covenant Agreement No. 24-112. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  REPORTS – CITY MANAGER. City Manager Mark F. Weinberg provided an update
  on the storm situation. He thanked Brian Walker, Emergency Services Manager, Police
  Chief Mark Fronterotta, the Public Works Crew, and all City employees who were out on
  the line and available for services during the unprecedented storm. He stated that the
  good news was that communications were regularly sent to the Mayor and Council
  Members throughout the past few days, and the City has sustained very little damage or issues
  related to the storm. The City Manager mentioned the tree that fell in Edward  Vincent Park,
  but the storm drains and roadways were clear, and the City remained safe. He also noted that the
  Office of Emergency Services was on duty monitoring and participated in regional calls with Los
  Angeles County, the National Weather Service,  and other partners that helped respond to
  emergencies. He discussed dispatching fire trucks, police vehicles, and other members of the city
  workforce to patrol the City to look for any problems. Finally, he addressed the ongoing status
  of the City’s condition via  social media, the website, and other forms of communication.

126  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, stated that it was great to
  see her colleague Council Member Padilla back on the dais. She also stated that he and his
  family was in her continued prayers. She reported about February being Black History
  Month and wished everyone a Happy Black History Month. She also reported about the
  Primary Election held March 5, 2024. She mentioned that ballots and sample ballet booklets
  have been mailed out and that drop boxes were opened on Thursday, February 1, 2024. She
  advised residents that it was safe to drop their ballots off at a drop box location and to make
  sure their ballots were signed. Additionally, she informed the residents of the drop box
  locations at Edward Vincent Park, Grevillea Art Park, and Rogers Park. Finally, she wished
  Councilwoman Faulk a Happy Birthday.

127  COUNCIL INITIATIVE

  Mayor Butts:

  MAYOR AND CITY MANAGER TO ACTIVELY PURSUE PARTNERSHIP WITH
  INGLEWOOD UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT (IUSD) AUTHORIZED. Initiative by
  Mayor James T. Butts, Jr., dated February 6, 2024, was presented recommending that the
  City Council authorize the Mayor and City Manager to actively pursue a partnership with
  the Inglewood Unified School District (IUSD) related to the renovation and use of the
  Inglewood Main Library.

  Mayor Butts presented a brief presentation regarding the partnership pursuit with Inglewood
  Unified School District (IUSD) related to the renovation and use of the Inglewood Main
  Library.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize the Mayor and City Manager to actively pursue
  partnership. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished

  2
 February 6, 2024

  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Ashley Taylor Vaughn, Aids Drug Assistance Programs (ADAP) Organizations, introduced
  herself as the new community organizer for the City of Inglewood. She stated that she looks
  forward to working with the City of Inglewood and invited the Council to the RX Takeback
  in April.

  Jessica Abaya, South Bay Community Service Provider, spoke about a free 8-week
  leadership development program for youth and young adults in Los Angeles County. She
  stated that the program was for adults between the ages of 16-20, and it prepares them for
  job readiness skills, leadership development, professional development, and financial
  literacy. Jessica noted that 19% of Generation Z, those born between 2006 and 2012,
  brought their parents to an interview last year because they felt unprepared. She also
  noted that the programs were available, and she wanted to introduce herself in hopes of
  bringing the program closer to Inglewood students. Finally, she mentioned the programs
  running out of Carson-Gardena and the Wilmington YMCA and how they are looking to build
  the program out in the community of Inglewood so students can reach the programs  as well.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the honor of Ervin Simonet’s 99th Birthday, and Charles Hypolite, at the hour
  of 2:41 p.m.

  Approved this 16th day of April, 2024.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
